lines: Non-healing wound on the plantar surface of the left foot present for two months with poorly controlled diabetes and numbness in feet.
The patient returns for evaluation of a plantar foot wound in the context of long-standing diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy and ongoing clinical trial participation for diabetic nephropathy.
He reports that the wound has been present for 2 months and has not improved with over-the-counter antibiotic ointments.
His diabetes has been poorly controlled, with a recent hemoglobin A1c of 9.2%.
He denies any fever or chills but notes numbness and tingling in his feet that has worsened over the past year.

The wound is located at the plantar aspect of the second metatarsal head and measures 2 cm in diameter with a calloused edge.

lines: Follow-up visit for non-healing ulcer on left medial malleolus that has improved with regular debridement and wet-to-dry dressings over three months.
The patient is a 61-year-old male with a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and peripheral neuropathy who returns for podiatry follow-up.
He has a non-healing ulcer on his left medial malleolus that he first noticed 3 months ago.

The ulcer initially had a moderate amount of slough and a foul odor, but after regular debridement and wet-to-dry dressings, the odor has resolved, and the amount of slough has significantly decreased.
